injuryReports.name: Zay Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran wideout played seven offensive snaps in Arizona's loss to the Rams last Sunday. With a boat load of injuries at the position, Jones figures to have a role for the foreseeable future. He has no fantasy appeal in this injury-ruined offense.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals elevated Jones from the practice squad Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. Joey Aguilar will operate as Johnson's backup, and Beck's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: Gaines will miss a fourth consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29. Hjalte Froholdt has cleared the league's concussion protocol and is slated to start at center against Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Hjalte Froholdt
injuryReports.returnComment: Froholdt was a full practice participant both Thursday and Friday, and he's progressed enough in his recovery to clear the league's concussion protocol. With Jon Gaines (ankle) ruled out, Froholdt should reclaim his starting job at center for Sunday's road tilt.
injuryReports.injury: Froholdt (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Zachary Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury he picked up in training camp in early August. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep but is not quite ready to return, so his next chance to make his 2026 debut is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Josh Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: With Carson Beck (back) not expected to practice Friday or play Sunday, Johnson appears in line to step into the starting quarterback role for Arizona. Johnson has a career 14:18 TD:INT across 50 regular-season appearances. The entire Arizona offense is one to avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions for Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson is expected to start Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams appears ready to return after missing the previous two games. He's been working as the Cardinals' starting left tackle after Paris Johnson (biceps) went on injured reserve following Week 4.
injuryReports.injury: Williams (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Walter Nolen III
injuryReports.returnComment: The defensive tackle was not able to practice Wednesday due to an illness. Now that he's back, he should be able to play Sunday against the Chiefs. Nolen has played on a majority of the defensive snaps in each game he's been available for this season, recording 25 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks.
injuryReports.injury: Nolen (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Budda Baker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the third consecutive week that Baker recorded at least six stops (and the sixth time this season). The veteran safety is up to 68 tackles (31 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games. Baker was held out of Wednesday's practice for rest purposes, so he should be available for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Baker posted six tackles (two solo) during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Mack Wilson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cardinals were blown out at home in Week 10, but Wilson came away from the loss with a season-high 10 stops while playing every single defensive snap. The veteran linebacker is up to 72 total tackles through 10 regular-season games, and he is three stops shy from matching his career-high that he set in 2024 with the Cardinals (over 16 regular-season contests).
injuryReports.injury: Wilson registered 10 tackles (six solo) during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Cody Simon
injuryReports.returnComment: Simon picked off a Matthew Stafford pass intended for Konata Mumpfield early in the second quarter, although the Cardinals' offense went three-and-out on the ensuing drive. It was the first interception of Simon's career, and the second-year linebacker has seen his snap count on defense steadily increase over the last few weeks. The 2025 fourth-rounder is up to 24 tackles (11 solo), one interception and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Simon recorded six tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: James Conner
injuryReports.returnComment: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Harrison Wallace III
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he played just five of the Cardinals' 35 snaps on offense, Wallace was able to come away with his first NFL reception in the third quarter. Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace recorded a nine-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Gardner Minshew II
injuryReports.returnComment: Though the procedure will bring an end to Minshew's season, he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 campaign. The veteran quarterback sustained the injury while making his lone start of the season Week 9 in Seattle, but he played though the elbow issue and completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 and is expected to lead the offense for the remainder of the season.
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Jordan Burch
injuryReports.returnComment: This move was a foregone conclusion, as head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Burch will miss the remainder of the campaign after suffering an MCL injury to his left knee. The defensive end finished his sophomore NFL season with 19 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, over 10 games. Burch will now look to get healthy in the hope of being ready for the 2027 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year contract extension worth up to $26.8 million. He didn't have much to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't get a target during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and he's caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't inspire much confidence heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Wingard
injuryReports.returnComment: Wingard picked up a wrist injury in the team's 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering from the injury. In Wingard's absence, Kitan Crawford and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson are both candidates to replace him as the team's starting free safety Sunday versus the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck as the starting quarterback. The offense struggled to move the ball and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first quarter. Fehoko's 26 offensive snaps led all Arizona wide receivers, and with Michael Wilson (neck) out for the rest of the season, he should continue to operate in an elevated role heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle.

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries. The Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, however. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).
injuryReports.injury: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Ryland provided all of the offense for Arizona in Week 10, making multiple field goals in a contest for the fourth time in the last five weeks. The kicker has rebounded well in 2026 after a challenging 2025 campaign, converting 22 of 24 field-goal tries over 10 contests so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland went 2-for-2 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.

injuryReports.name: Nick Vannett
injuryReports.returnComment: Vannett will be promoted to the Ravens' 53-man roster for a second consecutive week, and he will be available for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He played 20 snaps (14 on offense, six on special teams) and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens elevated Vannett from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Hawkins was a limited participant throughout the practice week, but it isn't enough for him to return in Week 11. The 29-year-old will miss his fifth straight game due to a knee injury. K'Von Wallace will continue to take reps in Hawkins' place.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Nnamdi Madubuike
injuryReports.returnComment: Madubuike popped up on the injury report as a non-participant in back-to-back practices due to a hamstring injury. With the 29-year-old out, John Jenkins will likely see a higher snap count on defense. Madubuike has 22 tackles (12 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass deflections in eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Olaivavega Ioane
injuryReports.returnComment: The offensive guard was limited during Wednesday's session. Ioane left Monday's loss to the Chargers with a shoulder injury and didn't return. The first-round pick out of Penn State has started all nine games he's played in this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ioane (shoulder/knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.

injuryReports.name: Marlon Humphrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Minter noted that after holding "internal conversations," he and the Ravens' brain trust decided to deactivate Humphrey for Week 11. Per Hensley, Humphrey acknowledged after Wednesday's practice that he regretted the comments he made in the podcast and issued an apology, so he's not expected to face any discipline beyond being held out of the matchup with the Panthers. Through the Ravens' first 10 games, Humphrey has tallied 40 tackles, nine pass breakups, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Personal

injuryReports.name: Adam Randall
injuryReports.returnComment: With the rookie fifth-round pick's 21-day evaluation window coming to a close Wednesday, Baltimore added him to the 53-man roster to ensure that he'll be available to play over the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 240-pound Randall has been a full participant in practices since Week 8 and should be healthy enough to play Sunday at Carolina, but it's unclear if Baltimore will make him active for that contest. Randall will likely slot in third on the depth chart at running back behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill, and Rasheen Ali is a key contributor on special teams who could be prioritized ahead of Randall on game days.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens reinstated Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve Wednesday, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Rasheen Ali
injuryReports.returnComment: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Lamar Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Roquan Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Kyle Hamilton led Baltimore with 10 tackles, and Smith was among three players who finished second with eight stops apiece. The veteran linebacker has hit the eight-tackle mark in four straight games and in eight of his 10 contests overall this season. Smith is tied for 11th in the NFL with 82 tackles on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Smith finished Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers with eight tackles (six solo).

injuryReports.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamilton is managing a hip injury but played all but one of Baltimore's defensive snaps Monday. He led the team with 10 stops, which were the second-most he's recorded in a contest so far this season. Hamilton seems to be on his way to a third consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign, as he has 70 stops through 10 games on the season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamilton posted 10 tackles (three solo) against the Chargers in Monday's Week 10 loss.

injuryReports.name: Mike Green
injuryReports.returnComment: Green's first sack came late in the second quarter, and he brought down Chargers QB Justin Herbert again early in the fourth. After registering 3.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, Green has already exceeded that mark with 5.5 sacks through 10 contests this season. His six total tackles in Week 10 also tied his career-high mark.
injuryReports.injury: Green racked up six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cuevas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cuevas had an immediate connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, reeling in at least three passes for the second time this season and the first time since Week 6. The tight end ranked fourth at his position with 11 offensive snaps, sitting behind Mark Andrews (40), Matthew Hibner (22) and Nick Vannett (14). Cuevas has now caught 13 of 16 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Cuevas caught all three of his targets for 37 yards during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Riley Patterson
injuryReports.returnComment: Patterson was signed by the Ravens on Wednesday, and he was able to make a 26-yard field goal as time expired in the first half before later adding a 36-yard make in the third quarter. With Tyler Loop (groin) set to miss at least two more contests while on injured reserve, Patterson will likely remain the team's starting kicker for the time being.
injuryReports.injury: Patterson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Justice Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Rashod Bateman
injuryReports.returnComment: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuryReports.returnComment: Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Mark Andrews
injuryReports.returnComment: According to Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site, Andrews confirmed after Monday's game that he's been playing through a broken left hand since Week 3, but he finally appears to be back to full health. Though he didn't miss any time due to broken hand, he was listed on the injury report from Weeks 4 through 9 before avoiding the report entirely for Week 10. He proceeded to deliver a season-best performance in starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett's team debut, eclipsing his previous-best mark in receiving yardage by 33 yards. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging after the Ravens' passing attack's moribund state over the prior two contests, and the veteran tight end could continue thriving in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers, especially now that he appears to have fully healed up from the hand injury.
injuryReports.injury: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Zay Flowers
injuryReports.returnComment: After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:11 remaining. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour note. Nevertheless, the fact Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game in the offense bodes well for Flowers' prospects as a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday approaches.
injuryReports.injury: Flowers brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and lost a fumble in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuryReports.returnComment: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects in this offense look bright if his first game is any indication, and he'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Kedon Slovis
injuryReports.returnComment: Slovis will operate as Baltimore's third option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Jacoby Brissett and backup Joe Fagnano are removed from the contest.
injuryReports.injury: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback Monday night versus the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Ed Oliver
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, Oliver notified the Bills' medical staff Saturday morning of pain in his oblique, but there's still optimism that the veteran defensive lineman will be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt. In the event that Oliver is inactive or operates on a snap count, more playing time on defense would be available for DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines and Landon Jackson.
injuryReports.injury: Oblique

injuryReports.name: Dee Alford
injuryReports.returnComment: Alford upgraded his practice participation in each subsequent session of Week 11 prep as he progressed through the five stages of the NFL's concussion protocol. The slot cornerback has been cleared by an independent neurologist and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Alford (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Dawson Knox
injuryReports.returnComment: Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he's trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox will operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches (on 20 targets) for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season games, and the Bills face a Dolphins defense that ranks 25th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.
injuryReports.injury: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Amani Hooker
injuryReports.returnComment: Hooker was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but the veteran safety was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. Hooker made his Bills debut against the Jets in Week 10, when he logged seven tackles (four solo) and one pass defense in a 31-12 win for Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Hooker (knee) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Damar Hamlin
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamlin was held out of practice in each of the first two practices of Week 11 prep due to a toe injury. He put together a limited session Friday to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play against the Dolphins, then Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin would operate as the Bills' backup safeties behind Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop for Sunday's AFC East tilt.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Jackson Hawes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hawes' practice reps during Week 11 prep were limited by a shoulder injury, which he may have picked up during the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets. Dalton Kincaid (thumb) is listed as doubtful, so that leaves Dawson Knox and Keleki Latu as the two healthy tight ends on the Bills' 53-man roster heading into the weekend. If Hawes is cleared to play, then he would operate as the TE2 behind Knox in the event that Kincaid is inactive.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Ray Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.
injuryReports.injury: Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Dorian Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams missed the last three practices with a calf injury he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. The 25-year-old is set to miss his first game since Week 5 of the 2025 regular season.  Kaleb Elarms-Orr should be in line to start in place of Williams, alongside Terrel Bernard.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Christian Benford
injuryReports.returnComment: Benford missed a trio of practices ahead of Week 11 after exiting early against the Jets with a groin injury. Sunday's game against the Dolphins marks the 26-year-old's second miss of the season. He has 33 tackles (23 solo) and eight pass deflections through eight regular-season appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bills are massive 16.5-point favorites at home against a Dolphins team missing its starting quarterback, so it presents an opportunity to give Kincaid a rest after he's been playing through injuries the last several weeks. Dawson Knox will remain an every-down tight end, with Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu stepping into elevated spots. The biggest beneficiaries likely will be DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in terms of target opportunities, though Buffalo should run all over this Miami defense.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Cole Bishop
injuryReports.returnComment: The safety was limited during Wednesday's session. Bishop has yet to miss a game this season, and it doesn't appear that streak will be snapped Sunday. He has 54 tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass breakups and a forced fumble in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Bishop (knee) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.

injuryReports.name: T.J. Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: TJ Parker
injuryReports.returnComment: Parker sacked his former Clemson quarterback Cade Klubnik twice in the Bills' blowout win. The rookie second-rounder called his shot, discussing his wishes to sack Klubnik while answering a question from Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo in late April.
injuryReports.injury: Parker accumulated five tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tyrell Shavers
injuryReports.returnComment: Shavers' 21-day evaluation window was set to close this week, so the Bills elected to add him back to the 53-man roster to ensure that he would be available to play this season. The wideout has been a full practice participant for the past two weeks, so he appears to be fully recovered from the torn ACL he sustained in January and should be available for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If active for the Week 11 contest, Shavers will likely slot in as a depth option at receiver behind the trio of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.
injuryReports.injury: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.

injuryReports.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too unpredictable to warrant weekly fantasy consideration.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ar'maj Reed-Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: It's not immediately clear when he suffered the back injury, but Reed-Adams will now have to sit out at least four games as he recovers. His absence leaves veteran Austin Corbett as Buffalo's undisputed backup plan at guard behind starters Alec Anderson and O'Cyrus Torrence.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Tyler Bass
injuryReports.returnComment: Bass made a 37-yard field goal in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker continues his perfect streak, having made all 20 of his field-goal attempts so far in 2026, with three such conversions coming from beyond 50 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Bass made his sole field-goal attempt and all four PATs in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Keon Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Shakir
injuryReports.returnComment: With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.
injuryReports.injury: Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: DJ Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore's 45-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter accounted for half of his team-high total in receiving yards. This was his most productive outing since Moore went for 100 yards and a TD in his Bills debut, and the veteran wide receiver has chipped in 216 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in three games since returning from a shoulder injury. Josh Allen and James Cook continue to lead Buffalo's offense with their legs, but Moore has re-established himself as Allen's top target in the passing game heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.
injuryReports.injury: Moore caught four of six targets for 90 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for four yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Josh Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen scored one-yard rushing touchdowns in the first and third quarters, bringing his season total up to 11 rushing TDs. He added his 13th touchdown pass of the campaign on a 45-yard strike to DJ Moore later in the third quarter, and Allen's fourth-quarter interception on third-and-long was basically an arm punt. Heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins, the star QB has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all but one outing this season.
injuryReports.injury: Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Brady Christensen
injuryReports.returnComment: The offensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened 18 days ago, so a decision will need to be made one way or another on activating him from injured reserve next week. Christensen hasn't played in a game this season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Simmons
injuryReports.returnComment: Simmons will be required to miss at least the next four games for Carolina. He's logged just six defensive snaps this season and another 206 on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Mike Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and was a full practice participant in all three Week 11 sessions. He's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, but his activated from IR indicates that the Panthers are confident that Jackson will be cleared to play.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks was a full practice participant in all three sessions during Week 11 prep. However, the third-year running back is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, and he's slated to miss his eighth consecutive game while recovering from a groin injury. Trevor Etienne, Anthony Tyus and AJ Dillon will continue to operate as the Panthers' backfield depth options behind Chuba Hubbard in the absence of Brooks, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Tommy Tremble
injuryReports.returnComment: Tremble put together a DNP-LP-LP practice log during Week 11 prep while managing a knee injury that he picked up during the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints in Week 10. Darren Waller (knee) also is listed as questionable, which leaves Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders as the Panthers' healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster heading into the weekend. Tremble's status for Sunday's game may not officially be known until 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when Carolina announces its list of inactive players.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Bobby Okereke
injuryReports.returnComment: Okereke hasn't practiced all week and will miss his third straight game due to a foot injury likely suffered in Week 8. Tyrel Dodson is slated to get another start.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Darren Waller
injuryReports.returnComment: According to Person, Waller told coach Dave Canales he's ready to play Sunday against Baltimore, so fantasy players should proceed as if Waller will be active. Waller's production has been all over the place this season, making him difficult to pin down as a reliable weekly fantasy option. He's more of a best-ball type of fantasy asset.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Will Lee III
injuryReports.returnComment: Lee missed the Panthers' last two games due to a hamstring injury. However, his full participation in Wednesday's practice indicates that the rookie fourth-rounder has fully recovered from his injury, and Lee should be back on the field for the Panthers against the Ravens on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Lee (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.

injuryReports.name: Tyrel Dodson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dodson finished second on the Panthers in stops behind Devin Lloyd (nine). It was the second straight start for Dodson as a result of Bobby Okereke being sidelined by a foot injury. If Okereke can't return for this Sunday's matchup against Baltimore, Dodson would figure to start and handle an every-down role again.
injuryReports.injury: Dodson logged seven tackles (two solo) Sunday in a 20-17 win over New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Devin Lloyd
injuryReports.returnComment: Lloyd was prolific as a tackler, leading Carolina with nine stops. He also put an end to the Saints' first offensive possession of the game with an interception of Tyler Shough. The pickoff was Lloyd's third of the campaign, a tally he's now reached in three of his five NFL seasons. With 63 tackles through eight contests, Lloyd is also on pace to reach triple-digit tackles for the fourth time.
injuryReports.injury: Lloyd registered nine tackles (five solo) and an interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Legette
injuryReports.returnComment: Legette made his return to the lineup after having been sidelined since Week 2 due to a knee injury, but he ended up playing just two snaps on offense. He will look to be more involved during next week's matchup versus the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Legette didn't produce any output in the boxscore during Carolina's win over the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: John Metchie III
injuryReports.returnComment: Metchie's only catch and target came late in the third quarter, as he logged four yards on a third-down play to help set up a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal. The veteran wideout had a streak of six games with multiple catches snapped in the Carolina victory. Metchie finished third among Panthers wideouts with 23 offensive snaps, and he's produced like a No. 3 receiver this year, logging no more than three catches and 40 yards in any of his eight games to date.
injuryReports.injury: Metchie caught his only target for four yards Sunday in a 20-17 win against New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Trevor Etienne
injuryReports.returnComment: Etienne again played second fiddle to starter Chuba Hubbard in Week 10 with Jonathon Brooks sidelined by a groin injury, and Etienne got his second-most touches of the season. His role on offense in Week 11 will depend on Brooks' status, but the vast majority of the Panthers' snaps at tailback will continue to go to Hubbard.
injuryReports.injury: Etienne took three carries for one yard and caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans. He also returned three punts for 43 yards.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuryReports.returnComment: Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired iced the game for the Panthers. The kicker made another field goal from 55 yards while also missing his first attempt of the night from 48 yards out. Fitzgerald moves to 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts and 18-for-23 on PATs so far during the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Fitzgerald made two of his three field-goal attempts and both PATs in the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Marco Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson has started the last three games at cornerback as a practice-squad elevation, and the Panthers have now made room for him on the 53-man roster. Wilson is set to start Sunday's game against the Ravens at outside cornerback opposite Will Lee (hamstring) or Corey Thornton. The Panthers released linebacker Nick Hampton in a corresponding move.
injuryReports.injury: The Panthers signed Wilson from the practice squad to the active roster Monday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Coker
injuryReports.returnComment: While it looked like Coker was going to be in line for a breakout 2026 season after his 8-138-2 receiving performance in the Week 1 opener, Coker has been held to 23 catches for 255 yards and one touchdown over his last seven games. At this point, he can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows something in the box score again. This was a pristine on-paper spot versus New Orleans in the dome, and next Sunday's home date against Baltimore won't be any easier.
injuryReports.injury: Coker failed to catch any of his four targets in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuryReports.returnComment: The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: Phillips has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Prior to the injury, he accumulated 10 tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks, across five regular-season games. His return will bolster the Panthers' pass rush alongside Patrick Jones, Trevis Gipson and Princely Umanmielen.
injuryReports.injury: Phillips (hamstring) is active against the Saints on Sunday, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Salvon Ahmed
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Kyle Monangai (toe) back from his toe injury for Sunday's game against New Orleans, Ahmed is up as the Bears' fourth running back, though he could be active ahead of Roschon Johnson, who played behind Ahmed in Week 9 against the Bucs.
injuryReports.injury: The Bears elevated Ahmed from the practice squad Saturday.

injuryReports.name: D'Andre Swift
injuryReports.returnComment: During Monangai's five-game absence due to a turf toe injury, Swift took on a majority share of the RB reps for Chicago, but even before that, he got a healthy dose of touches (79) en route to 395 yards from scrimmage and three rushing touchdowns through the first four weeks of the season. Meanwhile, Monangai turned his 65 touches into 363 total yards and three rushing TDs during that same stretch. Both players figure to be utilized liberally by head coach Ben Johnson in Week 11 and beyond, though Swift is the better weekly bet to surpass 50 percent of the offensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Swift will be rejoined in the Bears backfield by Kyle Monangai (toe) on Sunday against the Saints, Larry Mayer of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Kyler Gordon
injuryReports.returnComment: Gordon did not participate in practice coming off the Bears' bye week after picking up a shoulder injury in the team's Week 9 game against the Buccaneers. Week 11 marks the sixth game the 26-year-old has missed this season. Malik Muhammad, who is coming back from a toe injury, is expected to see more reps in Gordon's place.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Jeffery Simmons
injuryReports.returnComment: Simmons logged full participation in Friday's practice after beginning the week as limited with a knee injury. Since joining the Bears, the 29-year-old has 10 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass breakups on 119 defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Simmons has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Zavion Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: Thomas appears to have picked up an injury in the Bears' lead-up to Week 11, as he did not participate in Friday's practice. The rookie third-rounder acts as the team's top kick-return option. Should he not play, Josh Blackwell may take over duties on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Kyle Monangai
injuryReports.returnComment: After being listed as full on all three of the Bears' Week 11 practice reports, Monangai officially is in the clear for his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a right thumb issue and a turf toe injury. While working in tandem with fellow RB D'Andre Swift this season, Monangai has racked up 60 carries for 324 yards and three touchdowns and caught all five targets for 39 yards in four appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Monangai (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Tyrique Stevenson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevenson injured his hand during the Bears' Week 9 win over the Buccaneers. He had additional time to rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and given Stevenson's absence from Wednesday's estimated practice report, the fourth-year defensive back should suit up Sunday against the Saints. He has accumulated 34 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Stevenson (hand) was not listed on the Bears' estimated injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Luther Burden III
injuryReports.returnComment: Burden's status was up in the air for a bit with the Bears going on bye immediately after he sustained a concussion in a Week 9 win over the  Buccaneers, but he was spotted working out on the field with teammates Monday and has apparently cleared all five phases of the protocol. The second-year wideout looks like he'll be a full practice participant throughout Week 11, and he shouldn't face any playing-time limitations in Sunday's game versus the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Tuesday that Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.

injuryReports.name: Jaylon Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: In a game that featured seven turnovers between the two teams, Johnson's takeaway was arguably the most impactful of them all. He jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Cade Otton late in the third quarter, which Johnson returned 67 yards to the house for the second pick-six of his NFL career. The veteran defensive back is up to 27 tackles (21 solo), three pass defenses (including a pick-six) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson recorded three tackles (one solo) and a pick-six during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Cam Lewis
injuryReports.returnComment: Lewis jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Tez Johnson late in the second quarter, although the Bears offense turned the ball over on the very next play. It was the first interception of the season for Lewis and second of his career. The veteran safety is up to 35 tackles (25 solo) and two pass defenses across eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Lewis produced six tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Sam Roush
injuryReports.returnComment: Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.
injuryReports.injury: Roush caught both of his two targets for 23 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Roschon Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson recorded two tackles on special teams during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kalif Raymond
injuryReports.returnComment: Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs.

injuryReports.name: Cairo Santos
injuryReports.returnComment: It was an up-and-down night for Chicago's offense Sunday, as it moved the ball relatively well but committed five turnovers. Nevertheless, Santos got an opportunity to win the game on the last play of regulation with a 38-yard field goal, and it looked good from the moment it left his foot. Following a bye in Week 10, the Bears will play host to the Saints in Week 11, at which point fantasy managers might want to confirm the weather forecast in Chicago before locking Santos back into their lineups.
injuryReports.injury: Santos made both of his two field-goal attempts and converted all three of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Colston Loveland
injuryReports.returnComment: Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Rome Odunze
injuryReports.returnComment: Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards.

injuryReports.name: Case Keenum
injuryReports.returnComment: Keenum will once again operate as the team's emergency QB option in Week 9, making it four games in a row in that role. The 38-year-old will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Caleb Williams and backup Tyson Bagent are forced out of the contest.
injuryReports.injury: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Bears' emergency No. 3 quarterback for Sunday Night Football versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger has missed the past three games, but he has a chance to get back on the field against Washington. The veteran safety has appeared in just four games this season, logging 10 tackles (five solo) and a pass breakup.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Dalton Risner
injuryReports.returnComment: Risner was held out of practice all week due to injuries to both of his knees that he sustained in Week 10 against the Steelers. Ralen Rivers figures to start at right guard Monday in the absence of Risner, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Dax Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill was held out of practice all week while battling through an illness. He could still suit up Monday if he progress enough in his recovery, but if he's not cleared to play, then Josh Newton, PJ Jules and DJ Ivey would all be in line for more snaps in the secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but it looks like the fourth-year wide receiver will stay on injured reserve for at least one more week while recovering from a thumb injury. If he's inactive for Monday's game, then his next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: Burrow dealt with an illness during Week 11 prep, but with no injury tag the 2020 first overall pick has been officially cleared to play Monday night -- and per ESPN.com he is confident he will do so at "full strength." He's thrown at least three touchdowns in each of his last five outings, and over that span he has completed 77.6 percent of his passes for 1,624 yards, 20 touchdowns and three interceptions while turning 13 carries into 47 yards and two scores. The Bengals will face a Commanders defense that ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (244.8) and 30th in red-zone touchdown rate (71.9 percent).
injuryReports.injury: Burrow (illness) does not have an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Oren Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Myles Hinton
injuryReports.returnComment: The offensive tackle came down with the illness last Sunday morning and had to miss the Bengals' win over the Steelers that night. Hinton seems to be over the illness, and he should be ready to resume his role as a reserve lineman Monday night against the Commanders.
injuryReports.injury: Hinton (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Swayze Bozeman
injuryReports.returnComment: The linebacker suffered a broken forearm in Week 5 against the Dolphins but now has a maximum of 21 days to get ready for a return to action. He played just one defensive snap across the first four games of the season but was a fixture on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Forearm

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Fairchild
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Oblique

injuryReports.name: Joe Flacco
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.
injuryReports.injury: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Battle
injuryReports.returnComment: Battle ranked second on Cincinnati in stops. One of his six tackles went for a loss, and the 25-year-old also forced a fumble, though it was recovered by the Steelers. Battle has played every defensive snap in seven of the Bengals' nine contests this season, and he's collected 58 tackles and eight defensed passes, including three interceptions.
injuryReports.injury: Battle finished Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh with six tackles (four solo), one defensed pass and one forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.
injuryReports.injury: Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.
injuryReports.injury: Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Drew Sample
injuryReports.returnComment: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.
injuryReports.injury: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson converted a 24-yard field-goal attempt on the first drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to miss a 43-yarder in the second quarter of the contest, though the miss did not end up mattering to the final result of the game. McPherson is now 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts and 33-for-33 on PATs over nine contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson made one of his two field-goal attempts and all five PATs in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tahj Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both available, Brooks will continue to see limited playing time on offense.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry, but as is customary, his rushing opportunities were capped in a Bengals offense that typically takes a pass-heavy approach irrespective of game script. He still benefited from that philosophy, however, as he tied his second-highest reception total on the season while ending his seven-game touchdown drought by hitting paydirt twice. Brown will get another favorable opportunity to build on his production in Week 11, when the Bengals travel to D.C. for a matchup with the Commanders.
injuryReports.injury: Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards and brought in eight of nine targets for 39 yards for two touchdowns in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: Chase posted one of his signature 200-yard performances, with Sunday night's qualifying as the fourth of his storied career and marking his third instance accomplishing it against an AFC North rival. Needless to say, all three components of Chase's receiving line led the Bengals by a wide margin on the night as well, and after failing to hit the century mark in yardage in any of the first six games of the season, the star wideout has recorded at least 141 receiving yards in three straight. Chase is now up to a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets across nine games heading into a Week 11 Monday night home road matchup against the Commanders on Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Chase brought in 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: DJ Turner II
injuryReports.returnComment: Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Turner (ankle) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jashaun Corbin
injuryReports.returnComment: Corbin signed with the Cowboys' practice squad Nov. 4, and Saturday was his first elevation to the 53-man roster. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin will operate as Dallas' RB2 behind workhorse Javonte Williams. Corbin last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he appeared in six games as a member of the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Corbin was elevated from the Cowboys' practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: Thompson was a full participant in practice both Thursday and Friday, but the veteran safety is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve. He'll end up missing an eighth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he picked up in Week 3 against the Ravens. Thompson's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: DaRon Bland
injuryReports.returnComment: Bland was expected to miss multiple games due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the 49ers. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Dec. 27. Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant are both in line for larger roles in Dallas' secondary in Bland's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: P.J. Locke
injuryReports.returnComment: Locke was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol, and his absence means Markquese Bell will likely start alongside Malik Hooker at safety Sunday. Locke's next chance to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Donovan Ezeiruaku
injuryReports.returnComment: Ezeiruaku didn't play against the 49ers in Week 10 due to an ankle injury. He's avoided an injury tag for Week 11 after logging a full practice Friday, and his return means less rotational snaps at the edge rusher position will be available for James Houston and Von Miller. Ezeiruaku has 32 tackles (16 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Ezeiruaku (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuryReports.returnComment: Schoonmaker was held out of practice Thursday and Friday due to an illness, and he's drawn the questionable tag heading into the weekend. Jake Ferguson (knee) has already been ruled out, and with Schoonmaker under the weather, that leaves Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell as the Cowboys' two healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's contest. Michael Trigg could be elevated from the practice squad to the active roster depending on Schoonmaker's recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuryReports.returnComment: It will be the second game that Mingo will miss while recovering from foot and ankle injuries, which have prevented him from practicing over the last two weeks, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. In Mingo's absence, KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will be the Cowboys' rotational options at wide receiver behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jaishawn Barham
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuryReports.returnComment: The wide receiver had to sit for three games with a rib injury before coming back for last Sunday's loss to the 49ers, in which he fielded punts but not kickoffs. Turpin has 574 kickoff-return yards and 108 punt-return yards on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Turpin is expected to resume return duties on both kickoffs and punts Sunday against the Titans, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.

injuryReports.name: Jake Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' No. 1 tight end in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). However, George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets for Dak Prescott. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again top the depth chart in Week 11 against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.
injuryReports.injury: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Aubrey connected on 52-yard field goals in both the first and third quarters, although his PAT in the second missed wide left. It was the second missed extra-point try of the season for Aubrey and his seventh miss overall, although five of those failed kicks have come on field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards. The Cowboys will stay home for Week 11 against the Titans, who give up 26.6 points per game (27th in the NFL) and have yielded 40-plus points in each of their last two contests.
injuryReports.injury: Aubrey made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Israel Abanikanda
injuryReports.returnComment: Abanikanda made his 2026 regular-season debut against the 49ers in Week 10, when he operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Abanikanda finished that contest with two carries for eight yards and a two-yard catch on his lone target in what ended as a 46-40 loss for Dallas. With both Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) on injured reserve, Abanikanda figures to be elevated to the Cowboys' active roster for Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Abanikanda reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Booker
injuryReports.returnComment: Booker is expected to miss multiple weeks after injuring his ankle in the first half of Sunday's game against the 49ers, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. The 22-year-old may be able to avoid being placed on injured reserve with the Cowboys' bye coming in Week 14. T.J. Bass will likely slot into Booker's right guard spot.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Javonte Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams had a near monopoly on the Cowboys' running back touches, but he worked hard for everything he got against a talented 49ers front seven. The veteran back averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the seventh time this season, but he did eclipse 60 rushing yards for the third time in the last four games. Williams will take 692 rushing yards and nine rush TDs -- along with a 25-131-1 receiving line -- into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards and brought in his only target for four yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite his own impressive numbers, Lamb played second fiddle to George Pickens for a change, as the latter doubled up the former in receptions and did the same with a yard to spare in receiving yards. Nevertheless, Lamb still put together a solid performance that included his eighth touchdown reception of the season, a spectacular leaping one-handed one-yard grab late in the fourth quarter. Lamb now is up to five consecutive double-digit target tallies and has at least 70 receiving yards in four of the last five contests heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the vulnerable Titans defense.
injuryReports.injury: Lamb secured seven of 13 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dak Prescott
