The cornerback has now registered 46 total tackles (24 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson recorded four total tackles (three solo) and a pick-six in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Kevin Coleman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.

injuryReports.name: Brady Cook
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Zeek Biggers
injuryReports.returnComment: Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - Meniscus

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kaytron Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Gavin Bartholomew
injuryReports.returnComment: Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jeshaun Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Rodgers
injuryReports.returnComment: Rodgers popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quad injury. His practice reps were also limited in Friday's session, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Vikings announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings and Zemaiah Vaughn would likely be the top candidates to start opposite James Pierre if Rodgers is not cleared to play against San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Blake Cashman
injuryReports.returnComment: Cashman will end up missing one game (Week 10 against the Packers) while in the league's concussion protocol, and his return means Ivan Pace will revert to a rotational role at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Cashman has accumulated 76 tackles (41 solo), including a career-high-tying 4.5 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery across eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Cashman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Kyler Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: The quarterback lost his job to Kirk Cousins and will continue to manage a hamstring injury. Murray's availability will only matter moving forward if something happens to Cousins, either performance or injury related. Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer remain on the 53-man roster as backup options.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: T.J. Hockenson
injuryReports.returnComment: After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.
injuryReports.injury: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Eric Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Bo Richter
injuryReports.returnComment: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Jauan Jennings
injuryReports.returnComment: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jay Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jordan Addison
injuryReports.returnComment: Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Will Reichard
injuryReports.returnComment: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Myles Price
injuryReports.returnComment: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.
injuryReports.injury: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Tai Felton
injuryReports.returnComment: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Mason
injuryReports.returnComment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Kirk Cousins
injuryReports.returnComment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.
injuryReports.injury: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Justin Jefferson
injuryReports.returnComment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Metellus
injuryReports.returnComment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Carson Wentz
injuryReports.returnComment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.
injuryReports.injury: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.

injuryReports.name: DeeJay Dallas
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.
injuryReports.injury: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Smyth
injuryReports.returnComment: Smyth has been elevated from the Saints' practice squad for each of the team's last two games following the release of Daniel Carlson on Nov. 3. Smyth has gone 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 4-for-4 on extra-point tries in his two appearances, and his new deal means he'll be the Saints' kicker through the 2027 season.
injuryReports.injury: The Saints signed Smyth to a two-year contract Saturday, Michael McQuaid of NFL Ireland reports.

injuryReports.name: Asim Richards
injuryReports.returnComment: Richards suffered a significant knee injury in the Saints' Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The offensive tackle is expected to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, so his absence for Week 11 is no surprise. Mason Murphy is set to start at right tackle while Richards recovers.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Erik McCoy
injuryReports.returnComment: McCoy has not practiced since sustaining a biceps injury in the Saints' Week 9 clash with the Browns. The center will now miss consecutive games due to the injury, leaving Cesar Ruiz to start at center against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Biceps

injuryReports.name: Taliese Fuaga
injuryReports.returnComment: Fuaga did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions due to a knee injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The right tackle will now miss consecutive games due to the issue.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Martin Emerson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Emerson was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol. The fifth-year defensive back will not suit up for Sunday's contest, so Quincy Riley figures to be the top candidate to start at outside cornerback opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry in the absence of Emerson, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Pete Werner
injuryReports.returnComment: Werner was held out of practice all week while managing a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Panthers in Week 10. Despite the lack of practice reps, the sixth-year pro has drawn the questionable tag for Sunday's road contest. Danny Stutsman would likely start at inside linebacker next to Kaden Elliss if Werner is unable to play against Chicago.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Tyson
injuryReports.returnComment: Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Shough
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.
injuryReports.injury: Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.

injuryReports.name: CJ Donaldson
injuryReports.returnComment: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Decamerion Richardson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Thigh

injuryReports.name: Kaden Elliss
injuryReports.returnComment: Elliss was all over the field Sunday with a career-high 15 tackles (11 in the first half), which included an eight-yard sack on Bryce Young on the final play of the third quarter. Elliss has logged 10-plus tackles and a sack in back-to-back games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 56 stops (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across six regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Elliss recorded 15 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Lance
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Noah Fant
injuryReports.returnComment: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Devaughn Vele
injuryReports.returnComment: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.
injuryReports.injury: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Juwan Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Audric Estime
injuryReports.returnComment: Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Chris Olave
injuryReports.returnComment: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Alvin Kamara
injuryReports.returnComment: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.
injuryReports.injury: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.

injuryReports.name: Christen Miller
injuryReports.returnComment: Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: David Edwards
injuryReports.returnComment: Edwards' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but he avoided an injury tag for Week 10 after logging a full session Friday. He has started in each of the Saints' first eight games of the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Edwards (knee) does not have an injury designation against the Panthers on Sunday, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.

injuryReports.name: Kelvin Banks Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Banks was able to avoid an injury tag after logging a full practice Friday. Sunday's game will be his second since being activated from injured reserve Nov. 7 due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 2 against the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Banks (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.

injuryReports.name: Phil Mafah
injuryReports.returnComment: It's the second time this season that Mafah has been promoted to the 53-man roster, with the first instance being Week 10 against the Eagles. His elevation gives the Giants another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.
injuryReports.injury: The Giants elevated Mafah from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Likely
injuryReports.returnComment: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Malik Harrison
injuryReports.returnComment: Harrison missed the Giants' contest versus the Commanders in Week 10 because of a groin injury, but it appears he'll be able to return to game action in Week 11. Of his 141 total snaps so far in 2026, 136 have come on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Harrison (groin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jason Pinnock
injuryReports.returnComment: Pinnock left the Giants' game versus the Commanders in Week 10 with a back injury after just 15 defensive snaps, but it looks like he's back to full strength for Week 11. He should play a rotational role in the Giants' secondary during Sunday's contest against a run-heavy Jacksonville offense.
injuryReports.injury: Pinnock (back) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jameis Winston
injuryReports.returnComment: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.
injuryReports.injury: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Gipson
injuryReports.returnComment: Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Gipson was signed by the Giants off of Philadelphia's practice squad Monday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.

injuryReports.name: Micah McFadden
injuryReports.returnComment: McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.
injuryReports.injury: McFadden made 10 tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jevon Holland
injuryReports.returnComment: Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.
injuryReports.injury: Holland logged three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Ar'Darius Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.
injuryReports.injury: Washington accumulated seven tackles (five solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Arvell Reese
injuryReports.returnComment: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.
injuryReports.injury: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Dominic Zvada
injuryReports.returnComment: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injuryReports.injury: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.

injuryReports.name: Theo Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Mooney
injuryReports.returnComment: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.
injuryReports.injury: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.

injuryReports.name: Devin Singletary
injuryReports.returnComment: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Fields
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: J.J. McCarthy
injuryReports.returnComment: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Malik Nabers
injuryReports.returnComment: The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Sterling Shepard
injuryReports.returnComment: The move gives the Jets much-needed depth at wide receiver given the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. It will be the third elevation of the season for Shepard and first since Week 4 against the Bears, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Jets beyond Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Breece Hall
injuryReports.returnComment: "Obviously, [Hall] and Garrett Wilson are guys that we really try to target for the most part...Hall will end up getting a tick more [touches] because, again, he's our starting running back," Glenn said Friday. In his two outings since returning from a five-game absence due to a quad injury, Hall has turned 26 carries into 102 yards (3.9 YPC) while catching seven of eight passes for 93 yards, and he topped 100 scrimmage yards against the Bills in Week 10. Braelon Allen has reverted to RB2 duties in Hall's return, but the former has still been efficient with his touches and is still firmly in the mix for touches despite the return of Hall. The duo will face a Chargers defense Sunday that ranks 15th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (110.2) and limited Derrick Henry to 10 yards on 10 carries (albeit with two touchdowns) in a 23-20 win over the Ravens in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday that Hall could see a bump in touches for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Howie Kussoy of the New York Post reports.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Parham
injuryReports.returnComment: Parham practiced in all three Week 11 prep sessions, logging consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant Friday. Despite the upgrade to full participation, the offensive guard remains questionable for Sunday's contest, meaning his knee is likely still bothering him.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Harrison Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: Phillips started Week 11 prep as a DNP before logging consecutive limited sessions to end the week. If the defensive tackle is unable to suit up for Sunday's contest, Jack Heflin and Payton Page may see more rotational defensive snaps behind Darrell Jackson and Jowon Briggs.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: David Onyemata
injuryReports.returnComment: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and strung together three consecutive limited practice sessions. However, the veteran defensive tackle is not quite ready to come off IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29. Onyemata has not played since Week 2 against the Packers due to an abdominal injury.
injuryReports.injury: Abdomen

injuryReports.name: Trevin Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: A groin injury has prevented Wallace from playing in each of the Jets' last two games. He's questionable for Sunday's road game, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that the third-year linebacker is trending in the right direction heading into the weekend.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Geno Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Mason Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Isaiah Williams (ribs) also has been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.
injuryReports.injury: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Taylor could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Kenyon Sadiq
injuryReports.returnComment: In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) also will be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could translate to more targets in the passing game, but he's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.
injuryReports.injury: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Adonai Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooper was injured early in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, and Mitchell went on to see eight targets, as the Jets were playing catch-up most of the afternoon. They might be able to keep things closer against the 1-8 Chargers, though Los Angeles is still favored in the contest. Mitchell is a big-play threat as a WR4 for fantasy purposes.
injuryReports.injury: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, Mitchell is expected to play an elevated role on offense Sunday against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jarvis Brownlee Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: An illness prevented Brownlee from playing in the Jets' Week 10 loss to the Bills. His full practice Wednesday indicates that he is fully healthy and should be available for Sunday's road game against the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: Brownlee (illness) was a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Joseph Ossai
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Dane Belton
injuryReports.returnComment: Belton tied for third on the Jets with six stops. That's a total he's now reached in every game this season except Week 1. Belton ranks second among NFL safeties with 82 tackles on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Belton finished Sunday's loss to the Bills with six tackles (one solo) and one defensed pass.

injuryReports.name: Demario Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis' six tackles tied for third-most on the Jets. The veteran linebacker has been relatively consistent this season with between six and 10 stops in seven of his 10 games so far. Davis has 68 total tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through 10 games, putting him on pace for a 10th consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Davis posted six tackles (three solo) Sunday in a loss to Buffalo.

injuryReports.name: Jamien Sherwood
injuryReports.returnComment: Sherwood finished second on the Jets in stops Sunday, behind Harrison Phillips (10). Sherwood has notched at least eight tackles in five straight games, and he's hit the double-digit mark three times this season. The veteran linebacker ranks eighth in the NFL with 86 tackles through 10 games.
injuryReports.injury: Sherwood secured nine tackles (four solo) in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Jason Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders knocked in field goals from 41, 27, 22 and 48 yards out in Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all 12 of the Jets' points for a second straight week, performing the same feat in the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs. Sanders moves to 25-for-28 on field-goal attempts over nine contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts in the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Braelon Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.
injuryReports.injury: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Cade Klubnik
injuryReports.returnComment: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.

injuryReports.name: Garrett Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Zack Baun
injuryReports.returnComment: Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Will Shipley
injuryReports.returnComment: Shipley logged an LP/LP/DNP practice regimen during Week 11 prep, with Friday's absence attributed to an illness. He appears to be closing in on his first game action since Week 5, when he suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia, but his status for Sunday's matchup won't be confirmed until about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Assuming Shipley returns to action this weekend, he may serve as the direct backup to top RB Saquon Barkley.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Dontayvion Wicks
injuryReports.returnComment: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones logged a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury designation and return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He's contributed both on defense and special teams and has six tackles (five solo) and one pass defense across seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Michael Carter II
injuryReports.returnComment: An abdominal injury prevented Carter from playing in Week 9 against the Giants. He had extra rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Carter's return gives the Eagles a boost in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Carter (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Nolan Smith Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: An illness limited Smith's practice reps both Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year edge rusher has 17 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Britain Covey
injuryReports.returnComment: Covey was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but the veteran wide receiver has done enough to be cleared to return from a two-game absence due to a knee injury. He'll likely operate as the Eagles' top return option on kickoffs and punts while providing depth at wide receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Covey (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Makai Lemon
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former still will be heavily involved in the offensive game plan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. Joe Milton is getting the start at quarterback for a second straight contest, and the Eagles are facing a Steelers defense that ranks 30th in the NFL in receiving yards allowed per game (260.6). Over his last five outings, Lemon has put together a 27-247-1 line on 39 targets.
injuryReports.injury: Lemon will operate as the Eagles' WR2 against the Steelers on Sunday due to the return of DeVonta Smith (hamstring).

injuryReports.name: Saquon Barkley
injuryReports.returnComment: Barkley was able to put together a full week of drills during Week 11 prep, and while his current state is positive, he added that the time off isn't a "magic pill," indicating that he still has some residual effects from the hamstring injury that has lingered since he picked it up in Week 4. In his last appearance in Week 9 against the Giants, he handled a 58 percent snap share and turned his 13 carries into 22 yards and one touchdown. As for the rest of the Eagles backfield, Jaydon Blue is the only other option on the active roster, Elijah Mitchell is a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad, and Will Shipley (foot) may be activated from injured reserve Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Barkley (hamstring) told EJ Smith of PHLY Sports on Friday that he "feels better physically" after the team's Week 10 bye, and the running back doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Smael Mondon Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: DeVonta Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith followed up Wednesday's limited showing with an uncapped session one day later, thereby paving the way for his first game action since Week 6. Despite missing five of the last six contests due to a hamstring injury, he put together a 26-310-2 line on 41 targets in his four appearances this season. However, with Jalen Hurts (blood clots) out for the rest of the 2026 campaign, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from Joe Milton on Sunday against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (hamstring) practiced fully Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jihaad Campbell
injuryReports.returnComment: Campbell was sidelined for each of the Eagles' two contests prior to the Week 10 bye due to hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The second-year linebacker made the most of the extra rest courtesy of the bye, and he is on track to return against the Steelers on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Tanner McKee
injuryReports.returnComment: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.
injuryReports.injury: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.

injuryReports.name: Joe Milton
injuryReports.returnComment: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants, so Milton may need to show that he can avoid negative plays in Week 11 in order to guarantee himself additional starts.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.

injuryReports.name: Jaydon Blue
injuryReports.returnComment: It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change soon, as Will Shipley (foot - IR) had his practice window opened Monday. Elijah Mitchell has been promoted from the practice squad to help in the backfield each of the past three weeks, so he'd need to be signed to the active roster as well in order to suit up against Pittsburgh this Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: The Eagles signed Blue from their practice squad to their active roster Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Zach Ertz
injuryReports.returnComment: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.
injuryReports.injury: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.

injuryReports.name: Jeremiah Trotter Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Trotter recorded 11 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Darius Cooper
injuryReports.returnComment: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Arnold Ebiketie
injuryReports.returnComment: Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.
injuryReports.injury: Ebiketie will remain with the Eagles after his reported trade to the Bengals on Tuesday fell through and won't be completed, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.

injuryReports.name: Jake Elliott
injuryReports.returnComment: Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.
injuryReports.injury: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Eli Stowers
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.
injuryReports.injury: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Dallas Goedert
injuryReports.returnComment: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Max Hurleman
injuryReports.returnComment: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining on injured reserve and Roman Wilson (finger) officially listed as questionable, Hurleman is up as the Steelers' sixth receiver. He's never appeared in a regular-season NFL game.
injuryReports.injury: The Steelers elevated Hurleman from the practice squad Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Pittman was able to practice fully both Thursday and Friday, but he is not ready to rejoin the mix just yet -- which Pittsburgh confirmed by omitting Pittman from the list of roster moves it made Saturday. Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive Black Friday, when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Roman Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson has missed the Steelers' last four games while on injured reserve due to a left hand injury. He's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but his activation from IR indicates that the third-year wide receiver will suit up for the Steelers. Michael Pittman (foot) is staying on IR for at least one more week, so as it stands, Wilson slots in as the team's WR3 behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.
injuryReports.injury: Hand

injuryReports.name: Nick Herbig
injuryReports.returnComment: A hip injury prevented Herbig from participating in any of the Steelers' three practice sessions during Week 11 prep. The door was left ajar for him to play Sunday, but he'll observe the game from the sidelines, and his absence means Jack Sawyer will operate in an elevated role at edge rusher behind starters Alex Highsmith and T.J. Watt. Herbig's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Broncos on Friday.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: DeShon Elliott
injuryReports.returnComment: Elliott was able to string together back-to-back full practices to end Week 11 prep, which is an encouraging sign despite the questionable tag. His official status for Sunday's game may not be known until about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Steelers announce their list of inactive players. Robert Spears-Jennings and Brandin Echols would be the top candidates to start alongside Jaquan Brisker at safety if Elliott is not cleared by medical staff to play against the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Patrick Queen
injuryReports.returnComment: Queen put together an LP-LP-FP practice log during Week 11 prep, and despite the full session Friday, the veteran linebacker has been given the questionable tag for Sunday's game. If Queen cannot play against Philadelphia, then Cole Holcomb would likely start at inside linebacker alongside Payton Wilson, with Carson Bruener providing depth at the position.
injuryReports.injury: Hand

injuryReports.name: Gennings Dunker
injuryReports.returnComment: Dunker went to IR with a sprained MCL back in late September, but it now looks like he's close to being available again. The move opens a 21-day window during which Pittsburgh can officially activate him before he'd have to go back on the shelf for the remainder of the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Mason McCormick
injuryReports.returnComment: McCormick dislocated his ankle during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. The good news for the third-year pro is that he avoided a fracture and does not require surgery, so there's a chance he could return for the Steelers should the team qualify for the playoffs, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Brock Hoffman figures to start at left guard in McCormick's stead.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jaquan Brisker
injuryReports.returnComment: Pittsburgh gave up 38 points, so it wasn't exactly a stellar performance by the team's defense. However, three different Steelers players logged double-digit tackles -- including Brisker, who finished with 10. That's a season-high mark for the veteran safety, who has finished with at least six stops in all but one of his nine games so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Brisker notched 10 tackles (two solo) Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Payton Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson not only set a career high with his 19 stops, he also tied the NFL high mark by any player so far this season. The third-year linebacker has jumped up a notch as an IDP asset in 2026, as he's tied for sixth in the league with 88 stops through nine games. Wilson has also added a sack, three defensed passes (including one interception) and a fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson recorded 19 tackles (nine solo) in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Chris Boswell
injuryReports.returnComment: Boswell had an uneventful night, making his 45-yard field goal in the second quarter of the contest. The kicker moves to 19-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 17-for-17 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Boswell made his sole field-goal attempt and sole PAT in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Germie Bernard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Mason Rudolph
injuryReports.returnComment: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.
injuryReports.injury: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: DK Metcalf
injuryReports.returnComment: Metcalf's yardage total, modest as it was, led the Steelers on the night. The veteran receiver got there with the help of a team-long 32-yard catch, while his other reception was a 22-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter that Metcalf followed up with a two-point conversion. Metcalf has at least Sunday night's yardage total in three of the last four games, but he's still sporting an inefficient 35-432-2 line on 70 targets through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Eagles next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Metcalf brought in two of six targets for 54 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion catch in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Warren
injuryReports.returnComment: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Rico Dowdle
injuryReports.returnComment: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: Pat Freiermuth
injuryReports.returnComment: Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option (five in his nine appearances).
injuryReports.injury: Freiermuth recorded two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-18 loss in Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Rodgers
injuryReports.returnComment: The Steelers sat at 33 total yards of offense after three quarters, so the vast majority of Rodgers' output occurred on the team's three fourth-quarter possessions, two of which ended in touchdown connections with WR DK Metcalf (22 yards) and TE Pat Freiermuth (27 yards). Through nine games this season, Rodgers has tossed multiple TDs on five occasions, but he's also been held to less than 200 yards through the air three times. Rodgers will seek better results next Sunday in Phildadelphia.
injuryReports.injury: Rodgers completed 15 of 29 passes for 143 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed two times for minus-1 yard during Sunday's 38-18 loss at Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: Will Howard
injuryReports.returnComment: Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Harmon
injuryReports.returnComment: Harmon landed on IR in early October due to a foot injury. He was designated to return this past Wednesday and logged an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. Harmon is now set to return to the field Sunday night, though it's unclear if he'll be eased back into action in terms of defensive snap share.
injuryReports.injury: Harmon (foot) is active for Sunday's Week 10 clash against Cincinnati.

injuryReports.name: Brandin Echols
injuryReports.returnComment: Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Echols (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Nate Hobbs
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran cornerback remains on injured reserve but had been listed as questionable. He had his 21-day practice window opened 17 days ago, so the 49ers will need to make a decision on Hobbs next week. He's yet to play in a game this season.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: C.J. West
injuryReports.returnComment: The Niners also removed West's questionable tag, so he should be ready to play Sunday night against Minnesota. West played 41 percent of the defensive snaps during the first two weeks of the season before suffering his knee injury.
injuryReports.injury: The 49ers activated West (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Ji'Ayir Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown opened the week with back-to-back limited practices due to an ankle issue, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year safety has 51 tackles (28 solo) and three pass defenses in nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Dre Greenlaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Greenlaw was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a neck injury. He was a limited participant both Thursday and Friday, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford (chest) would be the top candidates to start at linebacker if Greenlaw is not cleared to play against Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Jordan James
injuryReports.returnComment: James' practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a calf injury. He was limited to kickoff return duties against the Cowboys in Week 10, and that role could be taken over by Deebo Samuel and/or Jacob Cowing if James is unable to play Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Mac Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones put together an LP-DNP-LP practice log while working through an illness, which puts him in jeopardy of not being available for Sunday's contest. If Jones is inactive, then Kurtis Rourke would operate as the 49ers' backup to Brock Purdy,
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Mike Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status until about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Renardo Green
injuryReports.returnComment: Green was not able to finish the 49ers' win over the Cowboys in Week 10 because of his back injury, but it now seems like he's back to 100 percent. He projects to play a significant role in San Francisco's secondary during Sunday's game against Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Green (back) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Isaac Guerendo
