injuryReports.returnComment: Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.
injuryReports.injury: Pectoral

injuryReports.name: Christian Kirk
injuryReports.returnComment: After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - Meniscus

injuryReports.name: Upton Stout
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Khalid Kareem
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Luke Gifford
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Chest

injuryReports.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
injuryReports.returnComment: This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aiyuk
injuryReports.returnComment: After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.
injuryReports.injury: Personal

injuryReports.name: Fred Warner
injuryReports.returnComment: Warner had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles while playing all 83 defensive snaps. The 29-year-old has now compiled 88 tackles (38 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Warner tallied 11 tackles (two solo) during San Francisco's win over the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Cowing
injuryReports.returnComment: Cowing was also sent back to receive two punts in Week 10, making a fair catch on one and allowing the other to go into the endzone for a touchback. He has now drawn just one target over the two games following his three-catch performance in Week 7, and his role in the 49ers' offense figures to shrink even further once veteran Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis, which could happen as soon as Sunday versus Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Cowing did not draw any targets during Sunday's 46-40 win at Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Demarcus Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Robinson's snap count was fourth-most among San Francisco's wide receivers, but his role in the offense shrunk due to the return of Deebo Samuel and the acquisition of Keenan Allen at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Brandin Cooks (coach's decision) was a healthy scratch for Week 10, and Robinson could join the former on the sidelines for Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22, if veteran wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) is cleared to return for that contest.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson played 21 of 65 offensive snaps (32.3 percent) but didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Watkins
injuryReports.returnComment: With Deebo Samuel still working his way back to 100 percent off his hamstring injury, Keenan Allen being eased in after his acquisition from the Colts and Mike Evans (Achilles) remaining inactive, Watkins' 44 snaps led San Francisco's wideouts. However, his three targets were a distant fourth on the team and represented just a 10.7 percent share. Allen will likely play more moving forward, and Evans is expected back in the bear future. Watkins doesn't have much fantasy appeal as an ancillary option.
injuryReports.injury: Watkins caught two passes for 49 yards on three targets in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Eddy Pineiro
injuryReports.returnComment: Pineiro made his only field-goal try from 28 yards in the second quarter. The kicker has now gone eight straight games without making multiple field goals, and his next chance to snap that streak will come in Week 11 against the Vikings' impressive defense.
injuryReports.injury: Pineiro made his only field-goal attempt and went 5-for-5 on PATs during Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Keenan Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen looked rejuvenated in his 49ers debut after coming over from the Colts at the deadline, finishing third in receptions and receiving yards and second in targets for his new squad in the wild win. Allen and Brock Purdy seemed to have instant chemistry despite having practiced on only three occasions coming into the contest, and the veteran receiver's production should have a good chance of spiking further down the stretch of the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Allen brought in five of seven targets for 61 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Baker Mayfield
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayfield missed three games earlier in the season due to a dislocated right thumb, and he injured his foot during the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. He was in a walking boot during Tampa Bay's bye and received treatment on his foot during Week 11 prep, although head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Friday that Mayfield is "trending in the right direction" to play against Detroit, per Pelissero. As it stands, Mayfield will be under center for the Buccaneers on Sunday, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels serving as the backup and Easton Stick operating as the emergency third quarterback.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Josh Hayes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hayes was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, but he is not quite ready to return from a knee procedure that he underwent in late August. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Yaya Diaby
injuryReports.returnComment: Diaby suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain during the Buccaneers' Week 8 win over the Falcons, and the injury prevented him from playing against the Bears in Week 9. He had additional time to recover thanks to the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, and he drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game after putting together an LP-LP-FP practice log. Diaby's return would result in less defensive snaps for David Walker and Al-Quadin Muhammad.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Antoine Winfield Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Winfield injured his ankle against the Bears in Week 9, and the extra week of rest courtesy of the bye was not enough for him to practice in any capacity during Week 11 prep. Ifeatu Melifonwu will likely start alongside Tykee Smith at safety in the absence of Winfield, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jalon Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayfield injured his foot in Week 9 against the Bears and sat out of Wednesday's practice, which resulted in Daniels taking all of the first-team reps during that session. Mayfield returned to practice Thursday and Friday as a limited participant, and it appears as though the 2018 first-overall pick will be under center for Sunday's game, which would result in Daniels operating as the backup and Easton Stick as the emergency third quarterback. Daniels started from Weeks 4 through 6 and went 1-2 over that stretch, when he completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions while turning 19 carries into 117 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Todd Bowles expressed optimism Friday that Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) will start against the Lions on Sunday, which would leave Daniels as the Buccaneers' QB2, Scott Smith and Brianna Dix of the team's official site report.

injuryReports.name: Easton Stick
injuryReports.returnComment: Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who was out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.
injuryReports.injury: The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Tykee Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Smith recorded seven tackles (four solo) and an interception in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Zyon McCollum
injuryReports.returnComment: The cornerback has been on an absolute heater in the interceptions department, as he's now recorded at least one pick in three straight games. After picking off Bryce Young and Michael Penix in back-to-back games, McCollum got Caleb Williams twice in Week 9. The four interceptions are a new career high for the fifth-year defensive back, who is now up to 35 tackles (28 solo), 11 pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: McCollum recorded five tackles (four solo) and two interceptions in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Alex Anzalone
injuryReports.returnComment: The Buccaneers picked off Caleb Williams four times, which included Anzalone's pick late in the third quarter that set up Tampa Bay in Chicago territory. Anzalone recorded four interceptions over his first nine NFL seasons, but he's already up to four picks in 2026, three of which have come over his last two outings. He enters the Week 10 bye with 44 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Anzalone posted two solo tackles and an interception during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Josiah Trotter
injuryReports.returnComment: Trotter led the Buccaneers in tackles in Week 9, when he played 59 of 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent). The rookie second-rounder has logged at least six stops in each of the first eight games of the regular season, and he enters the Week 10 bye with 76 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass defenses (including a pick-six).
injuryReports.injury: Trotter recorded eight tackles (five solo) during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Kameron Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Ted Hurst III
injuryReports.returnComment: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tez Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Sean Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.

injuryReports.name: Chase McLaughlin
injuryReports.returnComment: McLaughlin had a solid outing despite the loss, although all three of his field goals came from within 35 yards. Across his first nine outings of the season, the 30-year-old has yet to miss a kick, converting on all 22 field-goal attempts and all 18 extra-point tries.
injuryReports.injury: McLaughlin converted all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his extra-point tries during Tampa Bay's loss to the Bears on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cade Otton
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Bucky Irving
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - PCL

injuryReports.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Kenny Gainwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Emeka Egbuka
injuryReports.returnComment: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Harrell
injuryReports.returnComment: Harrell is being monitored following Saturday's accident. The third-year pro tore his ACL in a preseason game against the 49ers in mid-August, which led to him being placed on season-ending injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Tony Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: Adams logged a full practice Friday to draw the questionable tag, and he's now out of the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation from an independent neurologist. The veteran safety has accumulated 35 tackles (20 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Adams has cleared the league's concussion protocol and no longer carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Michael Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: The elevation of Carter gives the Titans extra depth at running back following the placement of Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve. Carter -- who has appeared in three regular-season games for Tennessee -- is listed as the fourth running back on the depth chart behind Tony Pollard, Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton.
injuryReports.injury: The Titans elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyjae Spears
injuryReports.returnComment: Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Carnell Tate
injuryReports.returnComment: Tate drew the questionable tag for Week 11 after a full practice Friday, and all signs point toward the rookie fourth-overall pick returning from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. With Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle, IR) out for the rest of the year, Tate will lead a Titans wideout group that also includes Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, Xavier Restrepo and Calvin Ridley. Tennessee faces a Dallas defense Sunday that ranks 26th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (239.7) and 30th in points allowed per game (28.2).
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Micah Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Kevin Winston Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Winston's practice reps were limited Thursday due to a shoulder issue, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag heading into the weekend. The second-year safety has 56 tackles (31 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Winston (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Anthony Hill Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with the questionable tag, Hill's full practice Friday indicates that the rookie second-rounder is trending in the right direction in his recovery from a neck injury, which prevented him from playing against the Jaguars in Week 10. His return would further bolsters a Titans linebacker corps that will welcome back Cody Barton, who also missed Week 10 while in the league's concussion protocol. Dorian Mausi would likely start at linebacker if Hill is not cleared to play against Dallas.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Cody Barton
injuryReports.returnComment: Barton strung together three consecutive full practices, and the lack of an injury tag indicates that the veteran linebacker has cleared the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing against the Jaguars in Week 10. Barton's return means less defensive snaps may be available for Dorian Mausi, although the latter could start at linebacker if Anthony Hill (neck) is not cleared to play against the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Barton (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Dallas.

injuryReports.name: John Franklin-Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: Franklin-Myers appeared on the Titans' injury report with a back issue Wednesday, but it doesn't seem like it was anything too severe. He should again play a prominent role on Tennessee's defensive line in a Week 11 tilt against the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Franklin-Myers (back) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Cedric Gray
injuryReports.returnComment: Gray was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. The third-year linebacker led the Titans in both total and solo tackles, and he also picked off a pass from Trevor Lawrence intended for Jakobi Meyers midway through the first quarter, although Tennessee's offense was not able to convert that takeaway into points. Gray is up to 46 tackles (26 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (one interception) through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Gray posted nine tackles (eight solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Fernando Carmona
injuryReports.returnComment: Carmona returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant in what was his first workout with the team since sustaining an ankle sprain in the Titans' Sept. 27 loss to the Giants. The Titans will have a 21-day window to evaluate him in practice, but once Carmona is deemed ready to return from IR, he could step into a starting role at either left or right guard.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Meanwhile Carnell Tate (shoulder) is slated to practice this week, and his potential return to action this weekend against Dallas figures to impact the playing time of Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Robinson's looming absence will free up snaps/targets in the slot, with Saleh noting Wednesday that he's looking forward to seeing what rookie slot option Xavier Restrepo can do with added opportunities going forward.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Julius Chestnut
injuryReports.returnComment: The fifth-year running back has suited up for all nine of the Titans' games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams as a member of the team's kick coverage and return units. He's played just two offensive snaps on the campaign and hasn't logged any carries or targets.
injuryReports.injury: Chestnut played all 25 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Restrepo
injuryReports.returnComment: A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.
injuryReports.injury: Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports.

injuryReports.name: Chimere Dike
injuryReports.returnComment: With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.

injuryReports.name: Daniel Bellinger
injuryReports.returnComment: The blocking specialist played 28 of 57 offensive snaps and was asked to block on 12 of those plays. His two-yard touchdown in the second quarter was Bellinger's first of the season. For the year, Bellinger has 11 grabs for 76 yards and the score on 18 targets across nine contests.
injuryReports.injury: Bellinger caught two of three targets for six yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Joey Slye
injuryReports.returnComment: Slye connected on field goals from 53, 54 and 50 yards during Sunday's loss, and he's now up to four makes from 50-plus yards on the year. He also made his way onto the highlight reel with a big tackle on a kickoff that forced the ball out of Josh Cameron's arms, although the Jaguars were able to recover the fumble. Through nine regular-season games, Slye has gone 15-for-16 on field-goal attempts and has made all 14 of his extra-point tries. Week 11 against the Cowboys could be a high-scoring affair, seeing as Dallas and Tennessee rank 30th and 27th, respectively, in points allowed per game.
injuryReports.injury: Slye made all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his extra-point tries during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also logged a tackle and forced a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Calvin Ridley
injuryReports.returnComment: Even though Carnell Tate (shoulder) was sidelined for a second consecutive week, Ridley was barely involved in the Titans' offensive game plan. Ridley's four offensive snaps were by far a season low, and his role figures to shrink even more given that Tate is expected to return for Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22. Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) could be sidelined for that contest, although those offensive snaps likely will go to Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and even practice-squad wideout Xavier Restrepo rather than Ridley.
injuryReports.injury: Ridley played four offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Gunnar Helm
injuryReports.returnComment: After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Elic Ayomanor
injuryReports.returnComment: While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Lucas Patrick
injuryReports.returnComment: Patrick was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed with reporters Saturday that Patrick cleared the league's concussion protocol and would start at center Monday, but the injury designation means that is not a guarantee. Nick Allegretti would likely start at center in the event that Patrick doesn't play.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Quan Martin
injuryReports.returnComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Martin (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Amik Robertson
injuryReports.returnComment: Robertson injured his ankle on the final play of Friday's practice, and his reps were limited during Saturday's session. If he's not cleared to play, then Mike Sainristil and Quan Martin would both be in line for more snaps in the Commanders' secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
injuryReports.returnComment: Croskey-Merritt has missed the Commanders' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury. He logged a trio of full practices this week and is officially questionable to play Monday, but it sounds like he'll be activated from IR ahead of the contest and make his return against the Bengals. During Croskey-Merritt's absence, Rachaad White has taken on a larger role in the backfield, but White is currently dealing with a heel injury and is also questionable to suit up Monday.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Treylon Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks was held out of Friday's practice while managing a foot injury, but he returned Saturday as a full participant, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Monday's contest. Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6 against the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Burks (foot) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Rachaad White
injuryReports.returnComment: White was added to the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue, and he followed it up with a DNP one day later before getting tagged ahead of Monday's matchup. At the same time, current IR member Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) completed a full week of drills and also is listed as questionable. If he's activated by Monday afternoon, he'll vie with Austin Ekeler and White for touches, assuming the latter avoids inactive status about 90 minutes before an 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.
injuryReports.injury: Heel

injuryReports.name: Laremy Tunsil
injuryReports.returnComment: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
injuryReports.injury: Triceps

injuryReports.name: Colson Yankoff
injuryReports.returnComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Luke McCaffrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.
injuryReports.injury: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Reaves
injuryReports.returnComment: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nick Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).

injuryReports.name: Frankie Luvu
injuryReports.returnComment: Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.
injuryReports.injury: Luvu recorded six tackles (two solo) and a forced fumble during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Sonny Styles
injuryReports.returnComment: Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).
injuryReports.injury: Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Drew Stevens
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.
injuryReports.injury: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Ben Sinnott
injuryReports.returnComment: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.
injuryReports.injury: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Austin Ekeler
injuryReports.returnComment: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.
injuryReports.injury: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Stefon Diggs
injuryReports.returnComment: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuryReports.returnComment: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.

sources.name: James Conner
sources.returnComment: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

00-0039910.injury: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

sources.name: Jayden Daniels
sources.returnComment: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

sources.returnComment: After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour note. health.injury: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

sources.name: Jayden Daniels
sources.returnComment: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

qbChemistry.method: Starter-linked weekly statistics; starting QB must supply at least 80% of team attempts and 15 attempts. Two-year recency half-life, eight-game pair and five-game comparison shrinkage; maximum 15% receiving change. Target allocation is conserved within each forecast team. No unsupported same-QB sample means no chemistry adjustment.
limitations: Starter-linked team-game splits are observational, not exact passer-target charting.
Role, opponent and scheme differences can confound historical splits.
Not yet validated out of sample; adjusted markets cannot pass the betting quality gate.

lineupPolicy.scope: Future forecast eligibility only. Missing rows are not actual zeros. No scoring probability or void-bet outcome is invented.

tdReport.orderMethodology: First and last TD fair odds come from separate player-game models trained on actual first/last scorer IDs, including defensive/return TDs in the event order and overtime. They use lagged opportunity and prior scoring-order rates; ATTD probabilities are not reused as first/last estimates. Game-level probability caps reserve mass for unmodeled scorers and no-TD outcomes. Book settlement rules may differ.

gameModelReport.model: Joint home/away score conditional-outcome forest v1

aggregate.calibrationScope: Home-win probabilities; ties are not wins. Reconstructed final-corrected public games, not archived sportsbook wagers.

scope: Original committed pregame model, inputs and recorded prices. Archived prices are not live. No postgame forecast reconstruction.
